Mossad carries out a covert assassination campaign targeting leaders of the Popular Front to Liberate Palestine, Fatah, and other Palestinian movements.

Mossad continues its campaign of covert assassinations of Palestinian leaders, including car bombs and amphibious operations.

Project Azorian
At the height of the Cold War, the US military endeavors to recover a sunken Soviet submarine from the depths of the ocean floor.

title: Back to the Blueprint
description:
Saltbox
In this episode, builder Marty Dunham heads to Connecticut. In Norwich, he examines the peculiar layout of a 300-year-old Saltbox house. And the woodchips fly as he fires up the chainsaw and helps finish up some structural repairs.

title: Back to the Blueprint
description:
Sears Home
In the early 1900s, buying a home was as simple as ordering it through the Sears catalog. Across the country over 75,000 Sears kit homes were built. Delivered in 30,000 pieces, they offered affordable and well-built housing to a growing middle class.

title: Back to the Blueprint
description:
Spanish Revival
The Spanish Revival (or Spanish Colonial Revival) home takes cues from all over the Mediterranean, mixes those with pre-Columbian buildings, drops it over a conventional stick frame, and makes a uniquely American home.

title: Back to the Blueprint
description:
Floating Home
More of our series focusing on historic houses. Today, host and contractor Marty Dunham helps restore and refloat the famous floating homes of Portland, Oregon.

title: The Big Build
description:
Lighthouse
Ever since sailors ventured into open waters, mariners have needed lighted signals to guide them safely through the night.

title: The Big Build
description:
Castle Tower
Our host, contractor Nick Mystrom, lands in Northern Idaho to erect a 2-story medieval castle tower in the same manner used by masons almost 1,000 years ago.

title: The Big Build
description:
Frontier Fort
Speed is the key word for this down-and-dirty build--Lewis and Clark, racing Oregon winter chill, built the 50 foot by 50 foot Fort Clatsop, a double-structure shelter with seven rooms, a sentry box, and parade ground, in just 15 days.

title: Boneyard
description:
Demolition
With America's cities and industrial centers rapidly aging and growing, thousands of buildings must be destroyed in order to be raised up again. These structures and their internal components will be transformed and recycled. There is great value not only in the structural materials, such as concrete, brick, and steel, but also in a wide array of vital, non-structural items like copper wire, stairways, plumbing, insulation, ventilation systems, and even glass. For many of the more grand structures, their hand-crafted and unique architectural features must be carefully removed and restored to new life. For all these activities there is a vast demolition industry to provide the expertise, skills, and the increasingly specialized tools to do the job.

title: Boneyard
description:
Garbage
The average American throws out more than four pounds of trash a day, nearly 300 million tons annually. An army of technologically advanced machines processes garbage, from the local collection trucks to the landfill compactors. In facilities called "Murfs," millions of tons of resources are given a second life. The water bottles you tossed in your recycling bin might become your new blanket. Electricity may be generated from the garbage you set out at your curb. Discover their unusual after-life as new products are created from garbage.

title: Story Feature
description:
The Big Dig
The Massachusetts Central Artery/Tunnel Project, a.k.a. The Big Dig, is the most amazing municipal construction project in U.S. history. Its objective--to replace Boston's decaying highway infrastructure with 160 new highway miles, half of which run underground and underwater. After 14 years construction, its cost--$11 billion!

title: The Most
description:
Survival/Fire/It's Mine, All Mine
Events covered include: Survival (USS Indianapolis, Alexander Selkirk, the Donner Party); Fire (Triangle Shirtwaist Factory Fire, Eternal Flame of Rome, Royster Tire Fire).

title: The Most
description:
Remarkable Battles
Mankind's most glorious moments and darkest hours occur during war. From the First Crusade's Siege of Jerusalem to the 1937 Rape of Nanking, relive some of war's worst massacres.

title: The Most
description:
Leaders/Mysteries/Spies
A look at: Leaders (longest reigning, most powerful woman, and deadliest.).

title: The Most
description:
Wastelands/Rock Legends/Sea Stories
Topics covered include: Wastelands (Most Toxic Town, Most Combustible River, Deadliest Smog); Rock Legends (Largest Monolith, Meteorite ALH84001, Hope Diamond); Sea Stories (America's First Mutiny, Royal Boat of Khufu, the Hunley).

title: The Most
description:
Incredible Disasters
Meet Mother Nature at her temperamental worst as we examine the most devastating events of the natural world. Deadly volcanic eruptions, virulent plagues, horrendous hurricanes, harrowing earthquakes, and appalling avalanches.

title: History's Lost & Found
description:
Episode 13
This week we take a look at Al Capone's bulletproof Cadillac and Imelda Marcos's 1,200 pair of shoes.

title: History's Lost & Found
description:
Episode 16
In this episode, see the first Apple desktop computer, Washington's handwritten schoolbooks, and the last New York City Checker Cab.

title: History's Lost & Found
description:
Episode 23
Artifacts found this week include: General Patton's staff car that ultimately caused his death and Robert Moog's 1967 synthesizer that turned the music business upside down.

title: Civil War Journal
description:
The Battle of Chattanooga
The saga of the sweeping battle that helped establish Gen. Ulysses S. Grant as a major leader. Follows the fight from lookout Mountain to Orchard Knob to Missionary Ridge, and demonstrates how Confederate Gen. Braxton Bragg blundered his way to defeat.

title: Civil War Journal
description:
Garden of the Dead: The Story of Arlington Cemetery
The story of how the Arlington, Virginia, home of Confederate General Robert E. Lee became a Union cemetery and later the official national military cemetery.

title: Civil War Journal
description:
Battlefield Medicine
The tale of the Civil War soldier's deadliest foe--disease. Typhoid and dysentery claimed more lives than battlefield wounds, and poor diet, unsanitary conditions, and emotional strain also took a deadly toll.

title: Civil War Journal
description:
Lincoln and Gettysburg
The story of the great battle's aftermath and the events leading to the dedication of the national cemetery and President Lincoln's immortal Gettysburg Address.

title: Civil War Journal
description:
War Crimes: The Death Camps
An examination of one of the most shameful sagas of the Civil War--the inhuman treatment of POWs by both the North and the South. Includes a look at facilities in the camps and the crimes committed against the prisoners.

title: Civil War Journal
description:
West Point Classmates
U.S. Military Academy classmates who fought on opposite sides of the Civil War.

title: Civil War Journal
description:
Dan Sickles: The General Who Got Away With Murder
Profile of the Union general who, before the war, became the first defendant in a murder trial to be acquitted on a plea of temporary insanity. Sickles killed a man he accused of having an affair with his wife.

title: Civil War Journal
description:
The Boy Generals
The remarkable tale of the very young men who rose to high rank in the war. Includes profiles of Galusha Pennypacker, who became the youngest general in American History, and Adelbert Amers, who won the Medal of Honor.
